content:
Let me carefully analyze the teaching examples to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

Looking at the examples, I need to compare:
1. Model forecasts vs true outcomes
2. How sentiment history correlates with these errors
3. What biases are present (lag, overshoot, under/over-forecasting, etc.)

Let me go through each example systematically:

## Example 1 (2025-01-13)
History: [64.43, 65.27, 64.26, 64.86, 67.69, 68.20, 69.68, 69.47, 71.56, 71.98, 73.00, 75.19, 75.94, 74.36, 74.04, 72.17, 73.46, 74.85]
True outcomes vs model:
- Day 1: forecast 76.15 vs actual 76.92 (model under by 0.77)
- Day 5: forecast 76.79 vs actual 79.26 (model under by 2.47)
- Day 10: forecast 77.89 vs actual 81.67 (model under by 3.78)
- Day 15: forecast 77.11 vs actual 80.96 (model under by 3.85)

The model is consistently UNDER-forecasting, especially as we get further into the future.

## Example 2 (2025-01-10)
Same data essentially:
- Day 1: forecast 74.22 vs actual 74.85 (under by 0.63)
- Day 5: forecast 75.16 vs actual 78.33 (under by 3.17)
- Day 10: forecast 76.80 vs actual 81.67 (under by 4.87)
- Day 15: forecast 77.47 vs actual 80.96 (under by 3.49)
